# History Department Meeting 2026-02-04

Spring term department meeting. Main item: whether to replace Medicine Through Time with Migration, Empire and People as the Year 10 thematic study. Decided 5-1 to switch all five Year 10 classes from September 2026. Partly reversed on 13 May 2026 ([[history-department-meeting-2026-05-13]]).

## At a Glance

> [!note]
> Vote 5-1 to switch all five Year 10 classes to Migration, Empire and People from September 2026. Desmond Hartigan voted against. Resources to be written over the summer term; Merrow's revised specimen papers expected "in the spring".

## Who and where

Wednesday 4 February 2026, 15:30 to 17:15, history office. Present: [[ruth-calder]] (chair), [[desmond-hartigan]], [[priyanka-sethi]], [[tomasz-zielinski]], [[amelia-fairweather]], me. Minutes: me.

## Item 1: thematic study option

Ruth's one-page proposal had gone round on 30 January.

**For switching** (Ruth, me, Priyanka):
- Migration links to the Year 8 enquiry on who came to Corrandale and to the empire enquiry in Year 9, recommendations 3 and 5 of the [[diverse-curriculum-audit]].
- Several ropeworks interviewees came to the town for work; the thematic study would let us use that at Key Stage 4 later, consent permitting.
- Medicine results are steady but not rising; we are teaching it from 2017 resources.
- Merrow told [[samira-benyoussef]]'s mailing list in December that revised Migration specimen papers would be out in the spring.

**Against** (Desmond):
- Medicine is examined well and our pupils do well on it. Why take a known risk with results?
- No specimen papers or mark scheme yet; writing schemes against a specification alone is guesswork.
- Five classes at once means everyone teaches it new, including Tomasz in his second year.
- Workload lands in the summer term, the same term as exam classes and the Year 9 scheme.

**Discussion.** Tomasz said he was keen but would need complete booklets by July. Amelia asked whether we could pilot first; Ruth said a split year group would need two exam entry codes and she was not sure the board allowed it. I estimated five booklets at about 15 hours each, so 75 hours shared across the department, and said we could have them ready by July. (That proved wrong: see [[migration-booklet-check-in-2026-05-06]].)

**Vote:** 5 for, 1 against (Desmond). Desmond asked for his reasons to be minuted; they are above.

## Item 2: moderation protocol, first month

The protocol adopted on 14 January ([[department-moderation-protocol]]) will first run on the March mocks. Sunil to draw the 10% sample.

## Item 3: Key Stage 3

Priyanka: Year 8 and 9 enquiry drafts on schedule for September. Ropeworks enquiry planning started with Luis Ortega ([[local-history-enquiry]]).

## Actions

- Ruth: tell [[kofi-asamoah]] and senior leaders; options booklet wording for Year 9 families unchanged (the subject is the same).
- Me: booklet plan and writing rota for five migration booklets by 25 February.
- Ruth: ask [[sunil-varma]] about entry codes, for information.
- All: no new Medicine resources for Year 10.

## Consequences

The vote set the plan recorded in [[thematic-switch-transition-plan-v1]]. Three months later, with specimen papers only out on 28 April and booklets about 40% drafted, the department cut it back to a pilot. Recap of the day: [[recaps/daily/2026/2026-02-04]].
